# TSDFGS

> **Version 3.0.0** keeps every function of v2 and adds 15 criteria. See
> [what changed](#what-changed-from-v2-to-v3).

TSDFGS helps you decide **which individuals to phenotype, and how
many**, before you build a genomic prediction model. Give it genotypes
(principal components or markers) and it searches for the training set
that optimizes a criterion.

## Find what you need

| I want to… | Go to |
|----|----|
| Install and run a first example | [Installation](#installation), [Quick start](#quick-start) |
| Pick the training set | [`optTrain()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/optTrain.md): [reference](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/optTrain.html), [guide](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/getting-started.html) |
| Decide how many individuals to phenotype | [`SSDFGS()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/SSDFGS.md): [reference](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/SSDFGS.html) |
| Read about the criteria | [Criteria overview](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criteria.html) and the table below |
| Check a criterion’s definition, source, or license | its page in the table below; [license review](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criteria-license-review.html) |
| Score a training set I already have | the `*_score()` functions, listed under [Reference](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/index.html) |
| Move code from v2 | [Moving from v2 to v3](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/migrating-from-v2.html) |

## Criteria

`optTrain(method = )` takes the name in the last column;
[`criteria()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/criteria.md)
returns this table in R. Each criterion has a page with its definition,
the original paper, the authors’ repository, and a license review. “Test
set” says whether the criterion uses the individuals to be predicted.

| Criterion | Type | Test set | `method` |
|----|----|----|----|
| [r-score](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-rscore.html) | Model-based | yes | `"rScore"` |
| [PEVmean (ridge, PCs)](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-pev.html) | Model-based | yes | `"PEV"` |
| [CD (ridge, PCs)](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-cd.html) | Model-based | yes | `"CD"` |
| [A-optimality](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-aopt.html) | Optimal design | no | `"AOpt"` |
| [D-optimality](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-dopt.html) | Optimal design | no | `"DOpt"` |
| [E-optimality](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-eopt.html) | Optimal design | no | `"EOpt"` |
| [CDmax (ridge, PCs)](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-cdmax.html) | Model-based | yes | `"CDmax"` |
| [PEVmax](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-pevmax.html) | Model-based | yes | `"PEVmax"` |
| [G-optimality (GOPTPEV)](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-gopt.html) | Optimal design | yes | `"GOpt"` |
| [MSPE of ridge regression](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-mspe.html) | Model-based | yes | `"MSPE"` |
| [GVoverall](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-gvoverall.html) | Genomic variation | no | `"GVoverall"` |
| [GVaverage](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-gvaverage.html) | Genomic variation | no | `"GVaverage"` |
| [Avg_GRM](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-avggrm.html) | Relationship | yes | `"AvgGRM"` |
| [Avg_GRM_self](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-avggrmself.html) | Relationship | no | `"AvgGRMself"` |
| [Avg_GRM_MinMax](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-avggrmminmax.html) | Relationship | yes | `"AvgGRMminmax"` |
| [CDmean](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-cdmean.html) | Model-based | yes | `"CDmean"` |
| [CDmean(v2)](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-cdmean2.html) | Model-based | yes | `"CDmeanV2"` |
| [Partitioning around medoids (PAM)](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-pam.html) | Clustering | yes | `"PAM"` |

The r-score is the criterion of [Ou & Liao
(2019)](https://doi.org/10.1007/s00122-019-03387-0). The others come
from the papers named on their pages. TSDFGS is released under GPL (\>=
3) and implements every criterion from its published definition in C++
(RcppEigen).

**What is tested.** Only three criteria are tested carefully: the
r-score, PEVmean, and CD, the criteria of v2.4.2. For all 12 routes of
[`optTrain()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/optTrain.md)
(with or without sub-populations, with or without a test set), the
training sets, scores, and score histories equal the output recorded
from v2.4.2.

The other 15 criteria are provided as they are described in their
papers, and the code runs without errors on all routes, but we have not
checked them carefully. We compared several of them with other
implementations (see the [license
review](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criteria-license-review.html)),
and each has a small test against a direct formula. This is not a
validation. Please evaluate them yourself on your own data before you
rely on them, for example by scoring training sets you know with the
matching `*_score()` function.

## Installation

This repository is the home of the package. Every push to `main` is
checked on Linux, macOS, and Windows (GitHub Actions), and the website
and the Docker image are built from it.

``` r

# Current version of the main branch (needs a C++17 compiler)
# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("oumarkme/TSDFGS")

# A given release, for example v3.0.0
remotes::install_github("oumarkme/TSDFGS@v3.0.0")

# Source package of a release (the file also attached to each GitHub release)
install.packages("https://github.com/oumarkme/TSDFGS/releases/download/v3.0.0/TSDFGS_3.0.0.tar.gz", repos = NULL)

# From CRAN, once the version is accepted there
install.packages("TSDFGS")
```

Without installing anything, use the Docker image (R, compilers, and
TSDFGS included):

``` bash
docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD":/work ghcr.io/oumarkme/tsdfgs:latest R
```

| Needed | Version |
|----|----|
| R | 4.0 or later (tested with 4.4.3 and with R-devel, release, and oldrel in CI) |
| C++ compiler | C++17 (GCC, Clang, or Rtools on Windows) |
| [Rcpp](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=Rcpp), [RcppEigen](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=RcppEigen) | Installed from CRAN with the package (tested with 1.1.2 and 0.3.4.0.2) |
| [ggplot2](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=ggplot2) | Optional; only for the figures of [`SSDFGS()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/SSDFGS.md) |
| OpenMP | Optional; for `multi.threads` and `threads`. Without it (default macOS compiler) the package runs on one thread and returns the same values |

The article [Installation and
environments](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/installation.html)
has the details for each system. Old versions are on the [releases
page](https://github.com/oumarkme/TSDFGS/releases).

### Version used in the manuscript

The manuscript (Ou & Liao, 2019) used TSDFGS 1.0, the first CRAN release
(2019-03-07). The r-score and the search of this package are the method
of that paper. To run version 1.0 itself, install it from the CRAN
archive:

``` r

install.packages("https://cran.r-project.org/src/contrib/Archive/TSDFGS/TSDFGS_1.0.tar.gz", repos = NULL, type = "source")
```

## Quick start

``` r

library(TSDFGS)
data(geno)                                   # 404 rice accessions, principal components
g <- as.matrix(geno)[, 1:15]

# 30 of the first 100 accessions to phenotype, to predict accessions 101-150
fit <- optTrain(g, cand = 1:100, n.train = 30, test = 101:150, seed = 1)
fit$OPTtrain                                 # rows to phenotype
r_score(g[fit$OPTtrain, ], g[101:150, ])     # criterion of the chosen set

# How many individuals are enough? (slow; use multi.threads = TRUE on Linux or macOS)
res <- SSDFGS(geno)
res$OC.fig
```

More in the [Getting started
guide](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/getting-started.html).

## Main functions

| Function | Purpose |
|----|----|
| [`optTrain()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/optTrain.md) | Find the optimal training set ([more](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/optTrain.html)) |
| [`SSDFGS()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/SSDFGS.md) | Find a reasonable training set size ([more](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/SSDFGS.html)) |
| [`r_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/r_score.md), [`pev_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/pev_score.md), [`cd_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/cd_score.md), … | Score of a given training set, one function per criterion |
| [`criteria()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/criteria.md) | List the criteria |
| [`FGCM()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/FGCM.md), [`nt2r()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/nt2r.md) | Building blocks of [`SSDFGS()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/SSDFGS.md) |

The packages [STPGA](https://CRAN.R-project.org/package=STPGA) (GPL-3)
and [TSODBG](https://github.com/spcspin/TSODBG) (GPL \>= 3) implement
several of the same criteria in R; we used them to check our results
(see the [license
review](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criteria-license-review.html)).

## What changed from v2 to v3

**New in v3.0.0:** 15 added criteria (see above), the
[`criteria()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/criteria.md)
function, and the `lambda` argument of
[`optTrain()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/optTrain.md).

**Nothing you call has changed.** All exported functions keep their
names and arguments, and the method is the one published in 2019.

|  | v2.4.2 | v3.0.0 |
|----|----|----|
| **Structure** | Search loop in R (12 copies of the same code), scores in C++ | R is the interface; scores and the search run in C++ (Rcpp and RcppEigen) |
| **Speed** | Reference | 2 to 174 times faster per iteration in our benchmark (see below) |
| **Scores** | Single precision (`float`) | Double precision; equal to v2 to about 1e-7 |
| **Reproducing v2** | n/a | `options(TSDFGS.legacy_float = TRUE)` with the same seed returns the v2.4.2 training set for all 12 routes (tested) |
| **Random search** | [`set.seed()`](https://rdrr.io/r/base/Random.html) only | Also `optTrain(seed = )` |
| **Result of [`optTrain()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/optTrain.md)** | `OPTtrain`, `TOPscore`, `ITERscore` | Same, plus `n.iter` and `converged` |
| **Small `min.iter`** | Error “the condition has length \> 1” below `5 * sqrt(length(cand) * n.train)` | Works |
| **Sub-populations without a test set** | `cand` had to be `1:nrow(geno)` | Any `cand` |
| **Input checks** | Cryptic errors | Clear errors for missing values, too large `n.train`, wrong row numbers |
| **Dependencies** | dplyr, ggplot2, latex2exp, parallel, Rcpp, RcppEigen | Rcpp and stats (ggplot2 optional) |
| **Figures** | ggplot2, red and blue | ggplot2 if installed, colorblind-safe Okabe-Ito colors |
| **Quality** | No tests | Tests, including regression tests against recorded v2.4.2 output |
| **Build and test** | n/a | Apptainer recipe in `env/` |
| **Website** | One page per function | New site with a guide and articles |

Speed on the rice principal components (one core, same seed and
iteration count; median of one run per case):

Milliseconds per iteration of
[`optTrain()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/optTrain.md)
(rice principal components, n.train = 50 to 100):

| PCs (p) | Case                         | v2.4.2 | v3.0.0 | Speed-up |
|--------:|------------------------------|-------:|-------:|---------:|
|      10 | CD, targeted, n=50, test=300 |  0.092 |  0.015 |     6.3x |
|      10 | PEV, untargeted, n=100       |  0.074 |  0.006 |    11.7x |
|      10 | r-score, untargeted, n=100   |  1.252 |  0.007 |   173.7x |
|      50 | CD, targeted, n=50, test=300 |  0.410 |  0.234 |     1.8x |
|      50 | PEV, untargeted, n=100       |  0.347 |  0.085 |     4.1x |
|      50 | r-score, untargeted, n=100   |  2.786 |  0.136 |    20.4x |
|     404 | CD, targeted, n=50, test=300 | 26.624 |  0.250 |   106.5x |
|     404 | PEV, untargeted, n=100       | 27.816 |  0.831 |    33.5x |
|     404 | r-score, untargeted, n=100   | 17.701 |  1.319 |    13.4x |

**Speed with 50 cores.** We ran 200 independent r-score searches
(untargeted, 100 of 404 rice accessions, 50 principal components) on 50
cores, with TSDFGS 1.0, 2.4.2, and 3.0.0. Versions 1.0 and 2.4.2 have no
multithreading, so they ran as 50 forked processes
([`parallel::mclapply`](https://rdrr.io/r/parallel/mclapply.html)). Each
violin shows the time of the 200 searches; the white dot is the median.
The median search took 5.07 s with version 1.0, 5.01 s with 2.4.2, and
0.29 s with 3.0.0 (17.6 times faster than 1.0). The whole job took 29.1
s, 29.5 s, and 1.9 s with the same forking, and 1.5 s with the OpenMP
threads of 3.0.0 (19.6 times faster than 1.0). The spread within a
violin comes from the stopping rule, which ends each search after a
different number of iterations.

![Time per search of 200 r-score searches on 50 cores. Medians: 5.07 s
(v1.0), 5.01 s (v2.4.2), 0.29 s
(v3.0.0).](reference/figures/speed-50-cores.jpeg)

Time per search of 200 r-score searches on 50 cores. Medians: 5.07 s
(v1.0), 5.01 s (v2.4.2), 0.29 s (v3.0.0).

**Parallel simulation.**
[`SSDFGS()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/SSDFGS.md),
[`FGCM()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/FGCM.md), and
[`nt2r()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/nt2r.md) run their
independent searches with OpenMP when you set `multi.threads = TRUE` or
`threads = n`. On a Linux server limited to 50 threads (100 searches,
404 rice accessions, 50 PCs, wall time):

| Method              | Threads | Seconds | Speed-up |
|---------------------|--------:|--------:|---------:|
| Serial              |       1 |     300 |     1.0x |
| `mclapply` (v2 way) |      10 |      32 |     9.3x |
| `mclapply` (v2 way) |      50 |      11 |      27x |
| OpenMP              |      10 |    31.5 |     9.5x |
| OpenMP              |      25 |    14.8 |      20x |
| OpenMP              |      50 |    10.1 |      30x |

OpenMP is about as fast as `mclapply`. What it adds: the same values for
any number of threads (tested), no forked copies of the data, and
Windows support. At 50 threads 100 searches are too few to keep every
thread busy. `optTrain(threads = )` lets one search use several threads:
the matrix products inside one search (only with several hundred
columns) and, for the targeted r-score and PEV search, the 30 candidate
sets of each generation.

The full list is in [NEWS.md](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/NEWS.md),
the article [Moving from v2 to
v3](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/migrating-from-v2.html) has
the details.

**Kept on purpose.** The r-score code multiplies the test set by
`1 - 1/n0` where a centering matrix may be intended. It stays as
published, so that results do not change.

## Example dataset

Zhao et al. (2011) published the rice genome data used as an example.
The raw dataset is on the [Rice Diversity
website](http://www.ricediversity.org/data/). The pre-arranged data are
in this repository and load with `data(geno)` and `data(subpop)`, or:

``` r

download.file("https://github.com/oumarkme/TSDFGS/raw/main/data/geno.rda", "geno.rda")
load("geno.rda")
```

## Reproducible environment

We tested v3 with R 4.4.3, Rcpp 1.1.2, RcppEigen 0.3.4.0.2, and GCC
16.2.0. All versions are pinned in `environment.yml`, and the Docker
image contains them. Use either of two ways to get the same software:

``` bash
# Docker image with R and TSDFGS installed (built and tested by GitHub Actions)
docker run --rm -it -v "$PWD":/work ghcr.io/oumarkme/tsdfgs:3.0.0 R

# conda / mamba environment with the pinned versions; then install TSDFGS from a clone
git clone https://github.com/oumarkme/TSDFGS.git && cd TSDFGS
mamba env create -f environment.yml
mamba activate TSDFGS
R CMD INSTALL .
```

Use a release tag such as `3.0.0` in your analyses, because `latest`
follows the main branch. The article [Installation and
environments](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/installation.html)
also covers a small conda environment, Apptainer, and building the image
yourself.

## Development

Build and test with the same software versions in an Apptainer image:

``` bash
env/build_sif.sh <work_dir>         # writes env/TSDFGS.sif (git-ignored)
apptainer exec --bind $PWD:/work --pwd /work env/TSDFGS.sif Rscript -e 'devtools::test()'
```

# Package index

## Find the training set

The main function. It searches the candidates for the training set with
the best criterion value.

- [`optTrain()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/optTrain.md) :
  Optimal training set determination

## Find the training set size

Simulate r-scores for several sizes and fit the operating curve.

- [`SSDFGS()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/SSDFGS.md) :
  Sample size determination for genomic selection
- [`FGCM()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/FGCM.md) : Fit
  logistic growth curve model
- [`nt2r()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/nt2r.md) : Simulate
  r-scores of each training set size

## Criteria: list

All criteria, with the name to give to optTrain(method = ).

- [`criteria()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/criteria.md) :
  List of training set criteria

## Score a given training set

Criterion values of a training set. One page per criterion under
Criteria in the top bar.

- [`r_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/r_score.md) :
  r-score
- [`pev_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/pev_score.md)
  : PEV score
- [`cd_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/cd_score.md) :
  CD-score
- [`pevmax_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/pevmax_score.md)
  : PEVmax score
- [`mspe_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/mspe_score.md)
  : MSPE score of ridge regression
- [`cdmean_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/cdmean_score.md)
  : CDmean score (GBLUP form)
- [`cdmean2_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/cdmean2_score.md)
  : CDmean(v2) score
- [`cdmax_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/cdmax_score.md)
  : CDmax score
- [`pam_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/pam_score.md)
  : PAM (k-medoids) cost

## Optimal design criteria

- [`aopt_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/aopt_score.md)
  : A-optimality score
- [`dopt_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/dopt_score.md)
  : D-optimality score
- [`eopt_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/eopt_score.md)
  : E-optimality score
- [`gopt_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/gopt_score.md)
  : G-optimality score (GOPTPEV)

## Genomic variation and relationship criteria

- [`gv_overall_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/gv_overall_score.md)
  : GVoverall score
- [`gv_average_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/gv_average_score.md)
  : GVaverage score
- [`avg_grm_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/avg_grm_score.md)
  : Avg_GRM score
- [`avg_grm_self_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/avg_grm_self_score.md)
  : Avg_GRM_self score
- [`avg_grm_minmax_score()`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/avg_grm_minmax_score.md)
  : Avg_GRM_MinMax score

## Example data

Rice genotype principal components (Zhao et al., 2011) and
sub-population labels.

- [`geno`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/geno.md) : Genotype
  information
- [`subpop`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/subpop.md) :
  Sub-population information

## Package

- [`TSDFGS`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/TSDFGS-package.md)
  [`TSDFGS-package`](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/reference/TSDFGS-package.md)
  : TSDFGS: Training Set Determination for Genomic Selection

# Articles

### All vignettes

- [License review of the
  criteria](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criteria-license-review.md):

  Which criteria TSDFGS includes, which it leaves out, and why.

- [Choosing a
  criterion](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criteria.md):

  The training set criteria in TSDFGS, one page each, and what recent
  comparisons found.

- [A-optimality](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-aopt.md):

  A-optimality minimizes the average variance of the ridge coefficients.

- [Avg_GRM](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-avggrm.md):

  The mean genomic relationship between the training set and the target.

- [Avg_GRM_MinMax](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-avggrmminmax.md):

  Combines the two: high relationship to the target and low relationship
  within the training set.

- [Avg_GRM_self](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-avggrmself.md):

  The mean relationship within the training set; minimizing it spreads
  the training individuals apart.

- [CD (ridge,
  PCs)](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-cd.md):

  CD is the squared correlation between true and predicted genetic value
  (reliability).

- [CDmax (ridge,
  PCs)](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-cdmax.md):

  CDmax is the largest coefficient of determination among the target
  individuals.

- [CDmean](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-cdmean.md):

  The mean coefficient of determination of the GBLUP contrast between
  each target individual and the target mean (Rincent et al.

- [CDmean(v2)](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-cdmean2.md):

  The heuristic form of CDmean from Chen et al.

- [D-optimality](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-dopt.md):

  D-optimality maximizes the information content of the training set,
  the determinant of the ridge information matrix.

- [E-optimality](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-eopt.md):

  E-optimality limits the worst-estimated direction: the inverse of the
  smallest eigenvalue of the information matrix.

- [G-optimality
  (GOPTPEV)](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-gopt.md):

  G-optimality minimizes the largest eigenvalue of the PEV matrix of the
  target, the variance in the worst direction.

- [GVaverage](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-gvaverage.md):

  GVaverage is the mean genetic variance of the training individuals,
  the trace of their relationship matrix divided by $`n`$ (TSDFGS
  returns the trace).

- [GVoverall](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-gvoverall.md):

  GVoverall measures the total genetic variation covered by the training
  set: the generalized variance of its relationship matrix.

- [MSPE of ridge
  regression](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-mspe.md):

  The expected mean squared prediction error of ridge regression for the
  target individuals (Chen et al.

- [Partitioning around medoids
  (PAM)](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-pam.md):

  The k-medoids cost: the training individuals act as medoids of the
  target.

- [PEVmean (ridge,
  PCs)](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-pev.md):

  The prediction error variance (PEV) measures how uncertain the model
  predictions are for the test set.

- [PEVmax](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-pevmax.md):

  PEVmax is the largest prediction error variance among the test
  individuals, so it protects the worst-predicted one.

- [r-score](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/criterion-rscore.md):

  The r-score is the expected Pearson correlation between predicted and
  observed values of the test set, written in closed form for ridge
  regression.

- [Getting
  started](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/getting-started.md):

  From a genotype matrix to a training set and a training set size.

- [Installation and
  environments](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/installation.md):

  Requirements, tested versions, and ways to install TSDFGS: R, Docker,
  conda, and Apptainer.

- [How the scores are
  computed](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/methods.md):

  The identities that make the v3 scores fast without changing their
  values.

- [Moving from v2 to
  v3](https://www.oumark.net/TSDFGS/articles/migrating-from-v2.md):

  What changed in v3, what did not, and how much faster it is.
